title: The GTA Heist That Actually Happened in Real Life
formula: Strange act (robbing a 100-million-dollar vault with hairspray) -> contradiction tease (only a sandwich can stop you; the sandwich shown, unexplained) -> video-game framing -> why (this weekend you rob it, 100 million dollars; threat: the vault on screen by 1 s) -> the perfect opponent (ten layers: heat, radar, magnets, a 100-million-combination lock) -> video-game framing (setup missions, two years) -> mission one: the fake dealer upstairs, guards stop looking -> mission two: the crew with nicknames, doubter Speedy ('We're gonna get caught') -> finale on Valentine's weekend: layer by layer (hairspray explained with 'You see' + breath on glasses, foam board, tape, aluminium plate, the lock nobody can explain) -> the loot (109 of 189 boxes) -> 'perfect heist' -> one job left: the trash -> reversal: Speedy panics and scatters it in the woods -> the litter-hating owner calls the police -> peak: receipt with your name, a videotape, a half-eaten salami sandwich with DNA -> doubter paid off (Speedy was right, because of Speedy) -> kicker (handcuffs, diamonds never found) -> loop (ten layers beaten with hairspray, undone by a sandwich)
loop: Lines 1-2: you rob a vault with hairspray, and only a sandwich can stop you. Last two: 'Ten layers of security. Beaten by hairspray. And undone by a sandwich.'

voiceNotes.speedy: Liam (ElevenLabs premade): young man, can go high and jittery: the anxious best friend who panics at everything

facts: True history: every stated fact is in sources.md. Main sources: Wikipedia 'Antwerp diamond heist' (which draws on the book Flawless, the police-side account) and CJR 2010 on the Wired 2009 story.

'You' = the inside man (Leonardo Notarbartolo, the convicted leader, a public figure in true facts only; never named in the narration, no invented thoughts beyond 'you visit until the guards stop looking').

Notarbartolo's own Wired account (hidden camera in the vault, insurance fraud, only $20 million) is disputed by the police and is NOT used as fact. How the combination lock was beaten is unknown, and the narration says so.
Speedy's two lines are invented, short and vague (Speedy is described in every account as anxious and paranoid; he scattered the trash).
GTA is named in line 3 as a comparison only. No game logos, game art, HUD or game characters: the 'heist mission' feel is our own (mission cards live on props: a notebook, a crew board).
Numbers: ten layers (the motif: hook, finale count, loop); a hundred million (combinations and dollars, the joke); 109 of 189 boxes; five days to the arrest.

lines.narration: You're robbing a hundred-million-dollar vault... with *hairspray*.
lines.spoken: You're robbing a hundred-million-dollar vault... with hairspray.
lines.scene: Cold open, two floors underground: a pink hairspray can in your hand hisses a cloud onto a small white sensor box high on a concrete wall. Hard cut at ~1 s: the giant round steel vault door, its big dial and spoked handle, lit by one cold ceiling lamp, a red alarm light blinking.
lines.camera: Macro on the can and sensor, hard cut to a low wide on the vault door
lines.gag: The sensor gets a cloud of glittery hairspray right in its face

lines.narration: And the only thing that can stop you... is a *sandwich*.
lines.scene: Smash cut: a half-eaten salami sandwich alone on dead leaves in a misty forest, lit from below like a horror-movie villain, a crow landing beside it. You (cut back) blink at it, confused.
lines.camera: Slow push in on the sandwich, hard cut to your confused face
lines.gag: A sandwich lit like a horror-movie villain

lines.narration: It's the biggest diamond heist in history, and you're running it like it's *GTA*.
lines.scene: You on the ladder under the sensor grin over your shoulder (scheming). A desk calendar on a shelf: February 2003, the 15th circled with a little heart. Behind the vault door's window: shelves of glittering boxes.
lines.camera: Push in on your scheming grin, tilt to the calendar
lines.onScreenText: Calendar: FEBRUARY 2003, a heart on the 15th
lines.gag: Your grin glints like a diamond
lines.spoken: It's the biggest diamond heist in history, and you're running it like it's G-T-A.

lines.narration: Ten layers of security: heat sensors, radar, magnets on the *door*.
lines.scene: Up on the street: a grey diamond-district building at night, a brass plate DIAMOND CENTRE. The camera drops through the floors (cross-section cut-away) to the vault two floors down; ten glowing layer rings light up around it one by one: a red heat cone, radar ripples, a blue magnet field over the door.
lines.camera: Crane down through a cross-section of the building
lines.gag: Ten glowing shields stack around the vault like an onion

lines.narration: And a lock with a hundred million combinations. One for every *dollar*.
lines.spoken: And a lock with a hundred million combinations. One for every dollar.
lines.scene: Macro on the vault dial: it spins on its own and a waterfall of numbers spills out of it and piles on the floor.
lines.camera: Macro on the dial, tilt down to the pile of numbers
lines.gag: Numbers pour out of the dial like a slot machine jackpot

lines.narration: So first, like every game, you grind two years of setup *missions*.
lines.spoken: So first, like every game, you grind two years of setup missions.
lines.scene: Your hotel room wall: a crew board of photos and string, a notebook with MISSION 1, MISSION 2, FINALE ticked off; a pile of empty espresso cups that grew over two years beside it.
lines.camera: Track along the board
lines.gag: The espresso-cup tower is taller than you

lines.narration: Mission one: a suit, a tiny magnifying glass, and the most serious face in *Belgium*.
lines.scene: You in front of a mirror in a sharp new suit, a jeweller's loupe screwed in one eye, practising a deadly serious face that keeps cracking into a grin.
lines.camera: MCU in the mirror, quick push on the loupe
lines.gag: Your loupe eye is three times bigger than the other one

lines.narration: Then you rent an office upstairs as a dealer. It comes with a box in the *vault*.
lines.scene: Your little office with a nameplate DIAMOND TRADING; a key on a tag VAULT slides across a reception desk into your hand.
lines.camera: Medium, insert on the key
lines.gag: The key slides into your hand like a casino chip

lines.narration: So you visit. Day one, the guard stares. Day ten, he nods. Day five hundred, he doesn't even look *up*.
lines.spoken: So you visit. Day one, the guard stares. Day ten, he nods. Day five hundred, he doesn't even look up.
lines.scene: The guard desk at the vault stairs, three passes on one locked framing: day one the guard stares you down; day ten he nods; day five hundred he waves you through without lowering his newspaper. A wall calendar behind him flips between passes.
lines.camera: Locked-off match cut on the same framing, three passes
lines.gag: By day five hundred the guard waves without lowering the newspaper

lines.narration: Mission two: the crew. The Genius does alarms. The Monster picks locks. The King of Keys copies any *key*.
lines.scene: Crew reveal, one MCU each on the beat: The Genius (glasses, tool roll, wires), The Monster (huge, tiny lock pick in giant fingers), the King of Keys (older, a ring of hundreds of keys on his belt, jangling).
lines.camera: Three hard cuts, each a quick push-in
lines.onScreenText: Crew board name cards: THE GENIUS · THE MONSTER · THE KING OF KEYS
lines.gag: The Monster's lock pick looks like a toothpick in his hand

lines.narration: And Speedy, your best friend... panics at *pigeons*.
lines.scene: Speedy (skinny, cap, sweat drop) jumps a foot in the air when a pigeon lands next to him on the street.
lines.camera: Medium, kick on the jump
lines.gag: Speedy jumps at a pigeon

lines.narration: We're gonna get *caught*.
lines.speaker: speedy
lines.scene: Speedy clutching your sleeve in the hotel room, eyes ring-shocked, sweating. You pat his shoulder, smug.
lines.camera: Two-shot, tight
lines.gag: Speedy's sweat drips onto your shoe

lines.narration: Then, on Valentine's weekend... it's *showtime*.
lines.scene: Night, the diamond district street: five figures walk out of the dark in a line toward the building, slow-motion, the Monster ducking under a shop awning.
lines.camera: Low tracking shot ahead of the crew
lines.onScreenText: A shop window full of Valentine's hearts
lines.gag: The heroic slow walk, and Speedy keeps checking behind him

lines.narration: Layer one, the heat sensor. You see, your hairspray coated its lens, like breath on cold glasses. It's *blind*.
lines.scene: Inside the dark vault corridor: the sensor box, its lens glazed and blurry. Insert: a pair of glasses fogging up from a breath, the same blur. Its red light stays dead as the crew walks under it.
lines.camera: Push on the sensor, hard cut to the glasses insert, match cut back
lines.gag: The sensor's view goes blurry like fogged glasses

lines.narration: Layer two: The Genius shuffles past the beam behind a foam board, like a kid behind a pizza *box*.
lines.scene: The Genius tiptoes sideways behind a big white foam board, only his eyes and fingertips showing, past a second sensor.
lines.camera: Side-on tracking at his speed
lines.gag: His fingers and eyes peek over the foam like a cartoon spy

lines.narration: Layer three, the light sensor. Beaten by... *tape*.
lines.scene: Macro: a strip of tape slaps over a little light sensor; its green light goes dark.
lines.camera: Macro, quick
lines.gag: One strip of tape, and the light just goes out

lines.narration: Layer four, the magnets: an aluminium plate taped on, so the alarm thinks the door never *opened*.
lines.spoken: Layer four, the magnets: an aluminium plate taped on, so the alarm thinks the door never opened.
lines.scene: The Genius tapes a shiny plate across the two magnet blocks on the vault door frame; the blue magnet field glows steady through it.
lines.camera: CU on the door frame, rack focus to the plate
lines.gag: The magnet field glows a happy steady blue

lines.narration: And the hundred million lock? It just... opens. Nobody knows how, even *today*.
lines.spoken: And the hundred million lock? It just... opens. Nobody knows how, even today.
lines.scene: The dial clicks, the spoked handle turns, the huge round door swings open, warm light and a sparkle pouring out over the crew's faces.
lines.camera: Low wide, slow push as the door swings
lines.gag: A sparkle of light floods out like a treasure chest

lines.narration: Inside: 189 boxes. By sunrise, 109 are open, and you're ankle-deep in *diamonds*.
lines.spoken: Inside: a hundred and eighty-nine boxes. By sunrise, a hundred and nine are open, and you're ankle-deep in diamonds.
lines.scene: The Monster cracks box after box down a wall of small steel boxes, doors hanging open down the rows; the floor is littered with gems, gold and papers up to your ankles.
lines.camera: Fast track down the box wall, crane down to your shoes in the gems
lines.gag: You wade through diamonds like a ball pit

lines.narration: No alarms, no witnesses. The perfect heist, with one job left: the *trash*.
lines.scene: Dawn in the safe house: you, proud, next to a heap of black garbage bags full of empty boxes, tape and food wrappers.
lines.camera: Medium on your proud face, pull back to reveal the garbage heap
lines.gag: The trash pile is bigger than the loot

lines.narration: So you and Speedy drive it to a forest by the *highway*.
lines.scene: A small car in morning mist, pulled over beside woods next to a motorway sign E19; the trunk full of bags.
lines.camera: Wide, then cut to the trunk opening
lines.gag: The trunk can barely close on the bags

lines.narration: But Speedy panics. Instead of burning it, he flings it all over the *woods*.
lines.scene: Speedy spins on the spot and hurls bag after bag into the trees; papers and wrappers rain down everywhere.
lines.camera: Medium, fast whip as a bag flies past the lens
lines.gag: Trash rains over the forest like confetti

lines.narration: Just *drive*!
lines.speaker: speedy
lines.scene: Speedy yanks you back to the car by the sleeve; you look back at the mess, worried.
lines.camera: Two-shot, handheld
lines.gag: Your face goes from proud to worried

lines.narration: The next morning, the old man who owns those woods finds it, and he HATES litter, so he calls the *police*.
lines.scene: An old man with a cardigan and a walking stick stares at the trash in his trees, face going red with steam puffs; he grabs his phone.
lines.camera: Medium on his face, he turns to the phone
lines.gag: Steam puffs out of his ears
lines.spoken: The next morning, the old man who owns those woods finds it, and he HATES litter, so he calls the police.

lines.narration: In the pile: envelopes from the vault, a videotape, and a receipt with your *name* on it.
lines.scene: Gloved police hands pull items out of the leaves one by one: a vault envelope, a videotape, a crumpled receipt; on the last, a name is circled in red.
lines.camera: Three macro inserts, hard cuts
lines.gag: The receipt is circled in red marker

lines.narration: And remember that sandwich? Half-eaten salami, covered in your crew's *DNA*.
lines.spoken: And remember that sandwich? Half-eaten... salami... covered in your crew's DNA.
lines.scene: The hero shot: a gloved hand lifts a half-eaten salami sandwich out of the leaves into a shaft of morning light, like a trophy; the bite mark faces the lens.
lines.camera: Slow push in on the sandwich, low angle, light flare
lines.gag: The sandwich gets a holy glow, like it's the real diamond

lines.narration: Speedy was right: you do get caught, because of *Speedy*.
lines.scene: Back in the hotel room: you turn slowly to Speedy; Speedy, mid-bite of another sandwich, freezes.
lines.camera: Two-shot, cut to Speedy frozen mid-bite
lines.gag: Speedy is eating another sandwich

lines.narration: Five days later, you're in *handcuffs*. Most of the diamonds are never *found*.
lines.spoken: Five days later, you're in handcuffs. Most of the diamonds are never found.
lines.scene: Your office door bursts open with police; cut to a newspaper on the guard's desk: HEIST OF THE CENTURY, the guard finally looking up.
lines.camera: Hard cut to the newspaper, push in
lines.gag: The guard lowers his newspaper at last

lines.narration: Ten layers of security, beaten by *hairspray*.
lines.scene: The cold-open sensor again, same framing, still glazed with hairspray.
lines.camera: Mirror of the opening macro
lines.gag: The fogged sensor, same framing as line 1

lines.narration: And undone by a *sandwich*.
lines.scene: Close-up on your face behind bars, deadpan; the sandwich in its evidence bag on a table, blurred behind you.
lines.camera: CU, hold
lines.gag: Your deadpan stare with the sandwich behind you
